mainTopic: How רבי יהודה treats doubtful vows: two answers to the contradiction from the pile case (רבא and רב אשי), and אביי splitting the תרומה and חרמים clauses of the משנה between two תנאים.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a contradiction between two rulings of רבי יהודה. He is strict on an unclear vow of תרומה, yet lenient on a doubtful נזירות in the pile (כרי) case. רבא answers that in נזירות the doubt is harsher than certainty. A doubtful נזיר can never shave or bring offerings, so a person does not mean to put himself into that doubt. רב הונא בר יהודה tests this with a נזיר עולם, and רבא shows the doubt is harsher there too. He then asks about a נזיר שמשון. רבא first says no such vow is taught. Then he accepts that if it is taught, there the doubtful vow would take hold. רב אשי gives a different answer: the lenient pile ruling is רבי יהודה quoting רבי טרפון, who holds that נזירות needs a clear statement. Finally the גמרא sees a new contradiction in the משנה between תרומה (doubt treated strictly) and חרמים (doubt treated leniently). אביי solves it by showing, from a ברייתא, that the חרמים clause belongs to רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.

steps.title: The end of the contradiction: where people are familiar, it is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes stating the contradiction. In רבי יהודה's תרומה case, where people know about the Temple-chamber תרומה, the vow is forbidden. So he is strict on doubtful vows.
steps.simpleTranslation: But where they are familiar, it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of a challenge. It shows that רבי יהודה is strict in a doubtful vow case, which clashes with his lenient ruling about a doubtful נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone vowed using the word 'תרומה' without saying which kind. רבי יהודה says that where people know about תרומת הלשכה, we must worry he meant that, so the item is forbidden. That is strict on a doubt, yet in the pile case רבי יהודה says the doubtful נזיר is not a נזיר. This line sets up רבא's answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: they are familiar with (here, people who know about the Temple-chamber תרומה)
forbidden
but this / here we see (points out an implication)

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new ruling. It is the second half of a contradiction the גמרא started before this point, and it shows רבי יהודה being strict on a doubtful vow.

phrases.english: But where they are familiar, it is forbidden!
phrases.notes: Familiar with the תרומה of the Temple chamber, so an unclear vow of 'תרומה' is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a contradiction begun before this point in the daf.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's lenient ruling that a doubtful נזיר (the pile case) is not a נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the תרומה case רבי יהודה treats a doubtful vow strictly, so why is he lenient on a doubtful נזירות?

steps.title: רבא: when the doubt is harsher than certainty, a person does not enter it
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that in the pile case a doubtful נזיר is worse off than a definite one. A definite נזיר can shave and bring his offering, but a doubtful one never can. A person does not mean to put himself into such a doubt, so he is not a נזיר at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Regarding the pile, רבי יהודה holds that whenever the doubt is stricter than certainty, a person does not put himself into the doubt. A definite נזיר shaves, brings an offering, and it is eaten, but for a doubtful נזירות he cannot shave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction. He shows that the pile case is special, so being lenient there does not clash with being strict on vows in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a doubtful vow is treated strictly, which is why the תרומה case is forbidden. In נזירות, though, a doubt traps the person forever. He can never shave, because he cannot bring offerings that might not really be holy. So we assume he never meant to accept a נזירות that might turn out that way. This makes it an exception in how the law is applied, not a change in the basic rule for doubtful vows.

keyTerms.meaning: a pile (of grain); here the case of someone who made his נזירות depend on how much grain was in a pile
its doubt is stricter than its certainty
a person does not put himself into a doubt
he shaves (to end his נזירות)
an offering

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets out a principle for vows: a person is assumed not to accept a vow on terms that would leave him trapped in a doubt with no way out.

phrases.english: Rava said:
regarding the pile, he holds
phrases.notes: This is the case of someone who said 'I am a נזיר if this pile has a hundred כור,' and then the pile was lost.

phrases.english: anything whose doubt is stricter than its certainty,
a person does not put himself into the doubt,
for whereas regarding a definite nazir,
he shaves and brings an offering, and it is eaten.
For his doubt, he cannot shave.
phrases.notes: A doubtful נזיר can't bring offerings that might not really be holy, so he can never shave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: נזירות is unique because its doubt is harsher than certainty.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה seemed to hold opposite rules about doubtful vows.
steps.terutzMaskana: He is strict on doubtful vows in general. In the pile case the person never accepted נזירות, because no one enters a doubt that is harsher than certainty.

steps.title: רב הונא בר יהודה asks about a lifelong נזיר
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה tests רבא's reason. Suppose the person said 'I am a נזיר עולם' (a lifelong נזיר). He never shaves at an end point anyway, so is the doubt still harsher than certainty?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה said to רבא: If he said 'I am hereby a permanent נזיר,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא's reason is being tested with a case where it seems not to work. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's whole reason was that a definite נזיר can shave at the end, but a doubtful one cannot. A נזיר עולם never finishes, so the definite and the doubtful one seem to be in the same position. If so, רבא's reason would not apply, and the question is whether רבי יהודה would rule strictly in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: a permanent, lifelong נזיר
I am hereby
what (is the law)?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said to Rava:
If he said 'I am hereby a permanent nazir,' what is the law?
phrases.notes: He means the same pile case, but with the person making himself a lifelong נזיר if the pile has a hundred כור.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer from step 2 with a case where it seems not to apply.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that a doubtful נזירות is harsher than a definite one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A נזיר עולם never shaves at an end point anyway, so the doubt does not seem any harsher than certainty.

steps.title: Even a lifelong נזיר's doubt is harsher
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that a נזיר עולם also has a way out that a doubtful one lacks. When his hair gets too heavy, a definite נזיר עולם may thin it with a razor and bring three animal offerings. A doubtful one cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: For a permanent נזיר too, the doubt is stricter than certainty. When a definite one's hair becomes heavy, he lightens it with a razor and brings three animals, but a doubtful one cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his reason. He shows that even for a lifelong נזיר, being doubtful is worse than being definite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A definite נזיר עולם is allowed to thin his heavy hair with a razor, along with bringing three offerings. A doubtful נזיר עולם cannot bring those offerings, because they might not truly be holy, so he can never thin his hair. רבא's principle therefore covers this case too.

keyTerms.meaning: his hair became heavy
he lightens (thins) it with a razor
three animals (the three offerings of a נזיר)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, רבי יהודה is lenient about a doubtful נזירות only because the doubt is harsher than certainty, and this is true even for a lifelong נזיר. So a person does not mean to accept such a נזירות.

phrases.english: He said to him: A permanent nazir too,
his doubt is stricter than his certainty,
for whereas a definite one, if his hair became heavy,
he lightens it with a razor,
and brings three animals.
Whereas his doubt, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ נְזִיר עוֹלָם נָמֵי סְפֵיקוֹ חָמוּר מִוַּדַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3 and upholds רבא's reason from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the principle still applies, using a different law (thinning heavy hair).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נזיר עולם never shaves, so his doubt seemed no harsher than certainty.
steps.terutzMaskana: A definite נזיר עולם can thin his hair with a razor and bring offerings, but a doubtful one cannot, so the doubt is still harsher.

steps.title: What about a vow to be a נזיר like שמשון?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה tests רבא's reason again with a נזיר שמשון, who never has any way out even when his vow is certain.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone said, 'I am a נזיר like שמשון,' what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה brings a new case to test רבא's reason. He asks about a person who vowed to be a נזיר like שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a doubtful נזיר is worse off than a definite one, because the definite one has some way out. A נזיר שמשון has no way out at all, not even thinning heavy hair. So here the doubt is no worse than certainty, and by רבא's reason the doubtful vow should take hold. Would רבי יהודה really say that?

keyTerms.meaning: A נזיר like שמשון: a lifelong נזיר who may never cut his hair at all
I am hereby (the opening words of a vow)
What (is the law)?

phrases.english: If he said, 'I am hereby a נזיר like שמשון,'
phrases.notes: This is still the pile case: he made this vow depending on how much grain is in the pile.

phrases.english: what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבא answered the נזיר עולם case, רב הונא בר יהודה pushes further with an even stricter kind of נזיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that a doubtful נזיר is worse off than a definite one
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A definite נזיר שמשון can never cut his hair, so doubt adds nothing harsher. By רבא's reason, would רבי יהודה then hold the doubtful vow takes hold?

steps.title: רבא: a vow of נזיר שמשון is not taught
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that no teaching recognizes a vow to be a נזיר like שמשון, so the question does not arise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: A נזיר like שמשון is not taught anywhere.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא avoids the challenge. He says there is no source that teaches a person can take on a נזיר שמשון vow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If no such vow exists, the case cannot be used to attack his reason. רבא is not explaining the case; he is denying that the case is real.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not taught (there is no ברייתא saying it)

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רבא is answering רב הונא בר יהודה.

phrases.english: A נזיר like שמשון is not taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 by denying that the case exists.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denying the premise: the case brought in the challenge has no source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A vow of נזיר שמשון works, so it would break רבא's reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: No teaching recognizes such a vow, so there is nothing to explain.

steps.title: But רב אדא בר אהבה says it is taught
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה pushes back: רב אדא בר אהבה said there is a teaching about נזיר שמשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But didn't רב אדא בר אהבה say that a נזיר like שמשון is taught?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה challenges רבא's answer. He quotes רב אדא בר אהבה, who says there is a source for נזיר שמשון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer depended on there being no such teaching. If there is one, the vow can work, and the challenge from step 5 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (so-and-so) say? (the opening of a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְהָאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה:
phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't רב אדא בר אהבה say:
A נזיר like שמשון is taught!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's answer in step 6 by bringing a report that the teaching does exist.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that נזיר שמשון is not taught
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אדא בר אהבה reports a ברייתא about נזיר שמשון, so the vow exists and the challenge stands.

steps.title: רבא accepts: if it is taught, it is taught
steps.stepSummary: רבא accepts the report. If there is such a teaching, he cannot argue with it, so his reason does not cover this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is taught, then it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא admits he has no answer. If the teaching exists, he accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא is accepting the conclusion that follows from his own reason. In a נזיר שמשון the doubt is not harsher than certainty, so if such a vow really exists, a doubtful one would take hold even according to רבי יהודה. רבא's principle still stands. It simply does not make the vow fail in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is taught, it is taught (I accept it and have no answer)

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not taking back his answer. He is accepting that if the teaching exists, a doubtful נזיר שמשון vow does take hold. That fits his reason, because in that case the doubt is not harsher than certainty. רב אשי's answer in the next step is a separate approach, not a rescue.

phrases.english: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
phrases.notes: In other words, 'If there really is such a teaching, I can't argue with it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 7 by giving in instead of answering it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: If a vow of נזיר שמשון is taught, then a doubtful one takes hold, since there the doubt is not harsher than certainty. רבא accepts this.

steps.title: רב אשי: that view is really רבי טרפון's
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers the contradiction in רבי יהודה differently. The lenient ruling in the pile case is not רבי יהודה's own view. He is quoting רבי טרפון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: That teaching is רבי יהודה speaking in the name of רבי טרפון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a new way to solve the contradiction from step 1. He says the lenient ruling in the pile case is רבי יהודה quoting his teacher רבי טרפון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On his own, רבי יהודה is strict about doubtful vows, as in the תרומה case. In the pile case he is only passing on רבי טרפון's opinion. So there is no contradiction within רבי יהודה's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: That one (that teaching)
In the name of

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: an apparent contradiction in one sage is solved by showing that one of the two statements is really his teacher's view that he reported.

phrases.english: רב אשי said:

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא — רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הִיא.
phrases.english: That one is רבי יהודה in the name of רבי טרפון.
phrases.notes: 'That one' means the pile case, where רבי יהודה ruled leniently.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר הָהִיא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב אשי offers a separate answer to the contradiction from step 1, different from רבא's answer in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different speakers: one statement is the sage's own view and the other is his teacher's view that he reported
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה himself ruled both strictly (תרומה) and leniently (pile), which contradicts itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lenient ruling belongs to רבי טרפון. רבי יהודה's own view is the strict one.

steps.title: The ברייתא: נזירות needs a clear statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא where רבי יהודה quotes רבי טרפון: none of them is a נזיר, because נזירות works only with a clear, definite statement.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי טרפון: None of them is a נזיר, because נזירות was given only through a clear statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב אשי by quoting the ברייתא. There, רבי יהודה reports רבי טרפון's ruling that a vow which is not clear does not make anyone a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון's reason is not about doubt being harsher. He says נזירות only takes hold when the person is completely clear about it. In the pile case the person did not know at the time of the vow whether he would be a נזיר, so the vow does not take hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A clear, definite statement of a vow
The status of being a נזיר

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי טרפון:
None of them is a נזיר,
phrases.notes: 'Them' are people in the full ברייתא who bet with each other using נזירות. Here the גמרא quotes only the ending.

phrases.english: because נזירות was not given
except through a clear statement.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב אשי's claim in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה reported a lenient view on unclear נזירות in the name of רבי טרפון
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: רבי יהודה in the name of רבי טרפון says none of them is a נזיר, since נזירות needs a clear statement
steps.whatToRemember: According to רב אשי, the lenient view in the pile case is רבי טרפון's, and his reason is that נזירות needs a clear statement (הפלאה). רבי יהודה's own view is strict.

steps.title: Then why does the case say the pile was stolen or lost?
steps.stepSummary: If the reason is that the vow was not clear, the person would not be a נזיר even if the pile were still there and measured. So why does the case say it was stolen or lost?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the case say specifically that the pile was stolen or lost?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב אשי's answer. It points to a detail in the pile case that now seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבי טרפון's reason, the vow fails because it was not clear when he made it. That is true whether the pile is lost or not. So the detail 'stolen or lost' seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why specifically (this detail)?
It was stolen or it was lost

phrases.english: If so,
why specifically that it was stolen or lost?
phrases.notes: In the pile case the pile went missing before it could be measured, so no one can know the answer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי מַאי אִירְיָא שֶׁנִּגְנַב אוֹ שֶׁאָבַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's answer based on the wording of the pile case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the lenient view is רבי טרפון's 'clear statement' rule
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that rule, the pile being lost makes no difference, so the case should not need to mention it.

steps.title: The detail shows how far רבי שמעון goes
steps.stepSummary: The detail 'stolen or lost' is there for רבי שמעון's side. Even when the doubt can never be settled, he holds the person is a נזיר, because a person does put himself into doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is to show you the strength of רבי שמעון's view. Even though it was stolen or lost, he holds that a person puts himself into a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the detail is not needed for רבי יהודה's side. It is there to show how strict רבי שמעון is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when the pile is gone and the doubt can never be resolved, רבי שמעון still holds the vow takes hold. He holds that a person does mean to put himself into a doubt. The 'stolen or lost' detail shows that he holds this even in the hardest case.

keyTerms.meaning: To show you the strength (of someone's view)
He holds
A person puts himself into a doubt

steps.whatToRemember: The pile case lists 'stolen or lost' to show how strict רבי שמעון is. He holds a person does put himself into a doubt, even one that can never be settled.
steps.confusionAlert: Notice the switch: the detail is explained for רבי שמעון, the strict side, not for רבי יהודה. The phrase 'a person puts himself into doubt' is the exact opposite of רבא's idea in step 2.

phrases.english: Rather, to show you the strength of רבי שמעון's view,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאַף עַל גַּב דְּנִגְנַב אוֹ שֶׁאָבַד,
phrases.english: that even though it was stolen or lost,
he holds that a person puts himself into a doubt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11 and defends רב אשי's approach.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The detail was written for the other side of the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'stolen or lost' detail must be needed for רבי יהודה's lenient ruling.
steps.terutzMaskana: The detail shows the strength of רבי שמעון's view: even with a doubt that can never be settled, the person is a נזיר.

steps.title: From the תרומה case: a doubtful vow is treated strictly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's ruling on unspecified תרומה and draws an inference from it: doubt in vows is treated strictly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says that unspecified תרומה in יהודה is forbidden, and so on. This implies that wherever people know about the chamber's תרומה, the vow is forbidden. So it seems a doubt is treated strictly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה and draws an inference from it. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will challenge that inference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who vows by 'תרומה' without saying which kind might mean the Temple chamber's תרומה, which would make the vow take effect. He might also mean the granary's תרומה, which would not. In יהודה people know about the chamber's תרומה, and רבי יהודה still forbids. So when a vow can be read either way, he takes the strict reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Unspecified; said without explaining which kind is meant
A portion set aside, either for the כהן or for the Temple chamber
They are familiar with it
Apparently; this shows that
A doubt is treated strictly

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Unspecified teruma in Judea, etc.
phrases.notes: כו׳ means 'and so on.' The משנה continues: in the גליל it's permitted, because people there don't know about the chamber's תרומה.

phrases.english: This implies: where they are familiar with it, it is forbidden.
Apparently, a doubt is treated strictly.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מַכִּירִין — אֲסוּרִין, אַלְמָא סְפֵיקָא לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new point in the משנה. It is a fresh look at רבי יהודה's approach to doubt in vows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the inference from רבי יהודה, an unclear vow that could be read as binding is treated strictly.

steps.title: The חרמים case seems to treat doubt leniently
steps.stepSummary: The next clause of the משנה, about unspecified חרמים, implies that a doubtful vow is permitted. This contradicts step 13.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה. Unspecified חרמים are permitted in יהודה but forbidden in the גליל, because people in the גליל don't know about the חרמים given to the כהנים. This implies that wherever people do know about them, the vow is permitted. So it seems a doubt is treated leniently!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges step 13 by pointing to the very next clause of the משנה, which seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unspecified חרמים could mean חרמים given to the כהנים, which would make the vow not take effect. They could also mean חרמים for the Temple, which would make it binding. In יהודה, where people know about the כהנים' חרמים, the ruling is permitted, which is the lenient reading. Since both clauses seem to be רבי יהודה's, he appears to contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (look at) the end of the משנה
Things dedicated by a חרם vow
חרמים that are given to the כהנים
A doubt is treated leniently

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the directions. In the תרומה case, 'they know it' leads to forbidden. In the חרמים case, 'they know it' leads to permitted. That flip is exactly the contradiction.

phrases.english: Say the last part of the mishna:
Unspecified dedications in Judea are permitted,
and in the Galilee they are forbidden,
because the people of the Galilee are not familiar
with the dedications given to the priests.
phrases.notes: These go to the כהן and aren't holy, so a vow that means them doesn't take hold.

phrases.english: This implies: where they are familiar with them, they are permitted.
Apparently, a doubt is treated leniently!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 13 using the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי יהודה treats a doubtful vow strictly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא implies that a doubtful vow is permitted, which is the lenient approach. That clashes with the strict approach inferred from the רישא.

steps.title: אביי: the חרמים clause belongs to a different תנא
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the סיפא follows רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, not רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: the end of the משנה is the view of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי resolves the contradiction by assigning the second clause to a different Sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no contradiction within רבי יהודה, because he never said the חרמים ruling. Two different תנאים can hold different views on doubt, so the strict inference from the תרומה case still stands for רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק הִיא.
phrases.english: The last part is the view of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: סֵיפָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the משנה between two תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both clauses are רבי יהודה's, so he contradicts himself on doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The תרומה clause is רבי יהודה's and the חרמים clause is רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's, so there is no contradiction.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the two clauses come from two Sages
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא attributes the תרומה ruling to רבי יהודה and the חרמים ruling to רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, which supports אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says unspecified תרומה in יהודה is forbidden. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says unspecified חרמים in the גליל are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the two rulings that appear together in the משנה are said by two different Sages. That is exactly what אביי claimed, so the חרמים ruling cannot be used against רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה treats a doubtful vow strictly, as the תרומה case shows. The lenient-sounding חרמים case is רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's view.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Unspecified teruma in Judea is forbidden.
Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Tzadok, says:
Unspecified dedications in the Galilee are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's answer in step 15 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That the חרמים clause belongs to רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that attributes the two rulings to two different תנאים
